newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia interest rate cut not a reward - Oppn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia interest rate cut not a reward - Oppn.

text.p: Australian Opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said on Wednesday the interest rate cut announced by the Reserve Bank of Australia on Wednesday was a result of the bank worrying about flattening economic growth.
"The rate cut is not a reward," Evans told reporters.

"It all depends on what the reason for the cuts are -- and the last two cuts have been a function of a Reserve Bank getting increasingly worried about the dampened flattening level of economic activity," Evans said.
He said economic growth at the moment was running closer to two percent instead of the 3.5 percent forecast in the budget, employment growth was sluggish and consumption was subdued.
"It's a bailout operation by the Reserve Bank for an economic boat which has been taking on more and more water and is in increasing distress," Evans said.
The bank said it would reduce official interest rates to 6.0 percent from 6.5 percent, a move which surprised markets as rates were last cut on November 6, by the same amount.
The bank said the rate cut reflected an improved inflation outlook, expecting underlying inflation to remain under 2.5 percent to June 1997 with a good outlook for 1997/98.
It also said the strength in the exchange rate had been a factor in the good inflation outlook.
The bank previously cut rates on July 31 and November 6 by half a percentage point on each occasion in response to lower inflation and moderate wages growth.
